title: Black-Owned Employers Top 200,000 but Hold 3.4% of US Firms | Across the Water, Ep. 23
lede: Ahead of Small Business Saturday on Nov 28, 2026, this episode looks at the numbers behind Black-owned businesses with a payroll. Census data show Black-owned employer firms rose from 124,004 in 2017 to 194,585 in 2022, and Brookings finds they passed 200,000 in 2023, with $249 billion in revenue and more than 1.8 million jobs. Yet they are 3.4% of US employer businesses, against a Black population share of 14.4%, and the Federal Reserve's latest credit survey shows a wide gap in who gets financed.
keyPoints: Black-owned employer firms grew 62% from 2017 to 2023, passing 200,000 for the first time, while all US employer businesses grew 3.3% (Brookings, Mar 10, 2026; Census ABS).
In 2023 they generated $249 billion in revenue, supported more than 1.8 million jobs and paid $69.8 billion in salaries; Black women owned about 79,000, up 78% since 2017 (Brookings).

Black Americans are 14.4% of the population but 3.4% of employer business owners; Brookings models parity at about 757,000 more firms, 6.3 million jobs and $824 billion in revenue (a scenario, not a forecast).

In the Fed's 2025 Small Business Credit Survey, 32% of Black-owned applicants were fully approved vs 57% of white-owned; 36% vs 17% were denied (Fed SBCS chartbooks via Hope Policy Institute, Aug 31, 2026).
Small Business Saturday, founded by American Express in 2010 and co-sponsored by the SBA since 2011, falls on Nov 28, 2026; the SBA counts more than 36.2 million US small businesses (SBA).
